# Rules-file SCHEMA keywords the engine legitimately spells as string literals.
#
# These are subtracted from donor_names.txt before TestNoDonorLiteralsInEngine-
# Sources runs. They are keys of the rules FILE FORMAT — the engine's own
# vocabulary, identical on every robot — that happen to collide with a word one
# donor also uses for a sense field or an action. The rules loader must be able
# to name its own schema; a guard that forbade that would be forbidding the
# wrong thing.
#
# The bar for adding a line here: the literal is a key or section name of the
# rules file format, spelled the same way for Reachy Mini and MicroDuck alike,
# and no channel or action name may be exempted on any grounds. Every entry
# carries its justification on the line above it.

# `[[react]]` / `[[inhibit]]` entries carry `enabled = false` as a TOMBSTONE:
# one line in the box-local overlay disables a shipped rule of that id without
# forking its body. It collides with microduck's `enabled` sense field.
enabled

# `[modes.<name>]` is the declarative parameter-set section of a rules file, and
# the loader's diagnostics name a single one of them "mode". It collides with
# microduck's `mode` sense field and its `mode` intent kind.
mode

# `active_mode` is the top-level key selecting which `[modes.*]` table is in
# force. Not itself a donor name — listed so a future substring-shaped matcher
# cannot silently start flagging it again, as one did before this file existed.
active_mode
